The final incident summary should use the audited figures from the official postmortem, not the informal engineering estimate.

- **Affected customers: exactly 17 active customer accounts/workspaces.** The official postmortem confirms through database transaction log audits that exactly 17 active customer accounts were affected [NL-013#NL-013-S02]. The engineering standup estimate of “maybe around 20 customers” was informal and preliminary [NL-022#NL-022-S03], and the postmortem later confirmed the exact count as 17 [NL-022#NL-022-S03]. The postmortem also states that internal engineering guesses should not be published and that the postmortem database audit is the sole authority for customer-impact metrics [NL-013#NL-013-S09].

- **Document upload impact: 142 document upload requests failed or remained stuck in the indexing queue.** The database audit identified 142 pending documents across the affected workspaces [NL-013#NL-013-S02].

- **Incident duration: 86 minutes.** The incident ran from 14:02 UTC to 15:28 UTC, a total service interruption of 86 minutes [NL-013#NL-013-S01].

- **No data loss; all pending documents were successfully processed after resolution** [NL-013#NL-013-S02]. Core querying/TutorChat on previously indexed files remained operational throughout [NL-013#NL-013-S01][NL-013#NL-013-S02].

**Why:** The “about 20” figure was a preliminary engineering ballpark that caused confusion [NL-013#NL-013-S09]. The final incident summary must rely on the postmortem database audit, which established the exact, verified figures of 17 affected customer workspaces and 142 affected uploads [NL-013#NL-013-S02][NL-013#NL-013-S09].
